pr_body:
Change to use the CLDR locale provider on JDK23+, rather than COMPAT

Also change several tests and doc examples that use the root locale to instead use english, as it is expecting the day-of-week names in english. Tests that use german I've changed to french, as that isn't changed between COMPAT and CLDR.

This fixes #109003, fixes #108855, fixes #108857, fixes #109188, fixes #109189, fixes #109200, fixes #108625

issue_context.title: JDK 23 changes how locales work in a way that breaks elasticsearch
issue_context.body:
There's various locale-based test failures when ES tests are run on JDK 23:

https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/109004
https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/108625
https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/108855

Tests are failing because the locale options are not being applied correctly.

However, when the following is run in a completely standalone class on jdk23:

`DateTimeFormatter.ofPattern("eeee", Locale.GERMAN).format(ZonedDateTime.now())`

it does correctly use the locale, and returns the German day name. When the same code is run inside an ES test, it _fails_ to apply the locale and returns the English day name.
comments: This might be due to removing COMPAT locale data in JDK23 - https://bugs.openjdk.org/browse/JDK-8325568
This is indeed caused by the removal of COMPAT in jdk23 - removing COMPAT locale on jdk 22 causes the same failures
